heard: Our universe could vanish in an instant with zero warning. This terrifying possibility stems from false vacuum decay, a metastable state where local stability could suddenly collapse. The theoretical framework for this catastrophic process was established by Sidney Coleman in 1977. Standard model calculations place the electroweak vacuum in this fragile metastable region. Calculations of the standard model vacuum lifetime estimate it exceeds 10 to the 65 to 10 to the 100 years. Yet researchers recently simulated these universe-destroying bubbles using a 5,564 qubit quantum annealer from D-Wave. Published in Nature Physics in 2025, these findings prove a bubble of true vacuum could expand at the speed of light. Because a bubble of true vacuum could expand at light speed, our universe could vanish in an instant with zero warning.
